statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of four representative localized marketing templates, consent entry, primary signed-out CTA, no-JS rendering, and HTTP 404 behavior.

page.notes: Public Business Profile acquisition site. The fresh UK session first redirects to consent.google.com. Representative pages are server-rendered and retain core content without JavaScript. Not covered: authenticated profile creation beyond Google Account sign-in, other product families (Ads, Merchant Center, Analytics), and every locale duplicate.

paths.description: Regional consent entry surface before the product site; checked symmetry and interruption.
Business Profile overview and primary acquisition landing page.
Retail audience/detail template representing a sector-specific landing page.
Services audience/detail template; selected for distinct illustrative cards.
Restaurant audience/detail template; selected for sector content and illustrative cards.

findings.summary: The localized Business Profile pages ignore the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: Across all four paths, prefers-color-scheme: dark matched, but body remained rgb(255,255,255), text rgb(60,64,67), and color-scheme was normal; dark screenshots are visually identical to light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens, using light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation does not opt into View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered probes found browser View Transition support, while the raw authored page contained no @view-transition or startViewTransition opt-in; sector links perform conventional full-document swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } for same-origin sector routes and suppress non-essential motion under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation does not expose scroll-state feedback.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile captures show persistent two-level chrome, but the authored output contains no scroll-state container-query or progress treatment to help orient users on the long page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky scroll-state container and a subtle scrolled state or progress cue on long landing pages.

findings.summary: A full-page consent interstitial blocks product content on first visit.
findings.evidence: The fresh-profile screenshot shows only “Before you continue to Google”; the actual Business Profile value proposition and CTA are inaccessible until Reject all or Accept all is chosen. Choices are symmetric, so this is interruption rather than deceptive consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Where policy permits, keep essential content visible and present consent as a compact semantic dialog/banner with equally prominent accept and reject actions.

findings.summary: Disclosure and menu UI is custom rather than using modern semantic primitives.
findings.evidence: Raw overview output contains no dialog, popover, or details elements despite dropdown navigation and an FAQ disclosure; controls are script-enhanced custom elements/buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Use details/summary for FAQ disclosure and popover/dialog primitives for transient menus where compatible.

findings.summary: Responsive changes are viewport-driven, with no container-query evidence.
findings.evidence: The same page adapts successfully at 360px, but stylesheet inspection found no @container rules, so reusable cards and navigation depend on page-level viewport logic.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable card/list regions and use size-aware @container rules for local adaptation.

findings.summary: The first keyboard-focus target has no visible focus indicator.
findings.evidence: The focus probe selected the first visible logo link and computed outline “none 3px” with no box-shadow; the mobile screenshot shows no visible focused state. Probes also found 1–4 sub-24px targets by template.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every focusable element a strong :focus-visible outline with offset and keep interactive hit areas at least 24px, preferably 44px for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Illustrative role=img components lack accessible text on two sector pages.
findings.evidence: axe-core reported role-img-alt on four ion-text-image elements on Services and four on Restaurants because role=img had no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title.
findings.suggestedFix: If informative, provide concise accessible names; if decorative, remove role=img and hide the wrappers from the accessibility tree.

findings.evidence: All four UK pages provide canonical URLs and localized language selection, but the DOM probe found zero link[hreflang] elements despite many equivalent regional/language variants. robots.txt allows /uk/ and points to sitemaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add reciprocal hreflang annotations for equivalent locale variants plus x-default, aligned with canonical and sitemap URLs.

findings.summary: The target omits Referrer-Policy and exposes only a narrow client-hints Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: Actual target headers include HSTS, nonce/strict-dynamic CSP, SAMEORIGIN, nosniff and COOP, but no Referrer-Policy; Permissions-Policy only enumerates UA client hints and does not explicitly restrict sensitive capabilities.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a deliberate Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin and explicitly disable unneeded sensitive capabilities in Permissions-Policy.
